source: Wei et al. (2022) Chain-of-thought prompting elicits reasoning in large language models
finding: A chain-of-thought prompt is a set of worked examples in context. Eight hand-written worked examples lifted a very large model on grade-school math.
numbers: PaLM 540B GSM8K: standard prompting 17.9%, chain of thought 56.9% (+39.0). Eight exemplars; three random GSM8K exemplar sets also tested.
limits: Gain appears mainly in very large models (>100B); small models gained little. Exemplars were few and fixed.
agent_relevance: The oldest LLM use of the worked-example idea. Treat any exemplar block as a worked example and test it at equal tokens (G7).

source: Min et al. (2022) Rethinking the role of demonstrations: what makes in-context learning work
finding: Replacing gold labels in few-shot demos with random labels hurt only a little. Format, label space and input distribution carried most of the gain.
numbers: Across 12 models and 16 demos per prompt, random labels cost 0-5% absolute (1.7% average on multi-choice tasks).
quote: replacing labels in demonstrations with random labels only marginally hurts performance
limits: Classification and multiple-choice tasks only, not multi-step math. Does not show wrong solutions are harmless in math.
agent_relevance: Part of a worked example may act as a format cue, not a source of knowledge. Do not credit the whole gain to solution content.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Towards understanding chain-of-thought prompting: an empirical study of what matters
finding: Exemplars with invalid reasoning kept most of the gain. Relevance to the query and coherent step order mattered much more than step validity.
numbers: text-davinci-002 GSM8K answer accuracy: standard 15.4, valid CoT 48.5, invalid reasoning 39.5 (over 90% of CoT intrinsic score kept), no coherence 23.1, no relevance 11.0. Bamboogle: CoT 45.2, invalid 39.4.
limits: Mostly one model in the main table; exemplars manually corrupted; arithmetic and multi-hop QA only.
agent_relevance: Library entries must keep the bridging objects and step order of the problem. Validity alone is not the active ingredient, but we still check validity in code.

source: Fu et al. (2022) Complexity-based prompting for multi-step reasoning
finding: Choosing worked examples with more reasoning steps beat random, centroid and handcrafted exemplars with only 8 annotated cases.
numbers: GSM8K / MultiArith / MathQA validation accuracy, 8 shots: random 52.5/86.5/33.0; centroid 52.0/92.0/32.0; complexity 58.5/93.0/42.5; retrieval from 10000 annotated cases 56.0/88.0/69.5. Average gain over Wei handcrafted CoT +5.3 (GPT-3) and +6.2 (Codex). Table rows were scrambled in the PDF text; mapping is by reading order.
limits: On GSM8K simple prompts did better on simple test items; on MathQA retrieval beat complexity by a lot. Complex exemplars cost tokens.
agent_relevance: Pick library entries by number of steps, not only by topic. Match exemplar complexity to the item when difficulty is known.

source: Gwak et al. (2026) Not the example, but the process: how self-generated examples enhance LLM reasoning
finding: Having the model create a related problem and solve it in the same turn helped. Reusing that same self-made example as a plain demo did almost nothing.
numbers: GPT-4o GSM8K: zero-shot 49.89, integrated 54.59, decoupled 50.49. MATH: 33.33, 37.86, 32.65. Llama-3.1-8B GSM8K: zero 12.06, decoupled 11.60, integrated 16.49. Multi-shot MATH: integrated 1/2/4-shot 35.19/38.93/38.24; decoupled 33.59/31.91/32.44. Five models. Dummy-integrated (irrelevant generated text) 33.82 vs about 32 on Llama-3.3-70B GSM8K.
quote: the advantage of self-generation prompting comes from the process of problem creation
limits: Absolute scores are low, so the baseline is weak. Attention analysis on one open model. Preprint.
agent_relevance: Matches the generation effect and self-explanation. Reading a stored worked example is weaker than making the model produce its own analogue inside the current turn. Favour generate-then-solve over paste-in.

source: Yasunaga et al. (2024) Large language models as analogical reasoners
finding: Asking the model to write its own relevant exemplars before solving beat 0-shot CoT and beat hand-written few-shot CoT.
numbers: GSM8K GPT-3.5-turbo: 5-shot CoT 75.0, self-generated 77.8 (best row). MATH: 33.0 to 37.3. PaLM2 GSM8K 60.8 to 81.7; MATH 27.1 to 34.8. K=1 exemplar worse than K>=3 (GSM8K 76.1 vs 77.5); best at K=3 or 5.
limits: Small models (curie-001, davinci-001) did better with retrieved labelled exemplars. Self-generation needs a strong model. Table cells scrambled in PDF text; rows mapped by order.
agent_relevance: Self-made worked examples need a strong enough model; for a weak one keep a curated library. Use K of 3 to 5, never 1.

source: Chen et al. (2024) Relevant or random: can LLMs truly perform analogical reasoning?
finding: Self-generated relevant exemplars did not beat unrelated self-generated ones on math. Correctness of the exemplar mattered most.
numbers: GPT-3.5 GSM8K/MATH: relevant 71.5/33.3; N/A 75.5/36.1; random-bio 75.3/34.6; ICL-bio 77.9/34.9; ICL-math 75.7/36.8. GPT-4o-mini GSM8K: relevant 90.7, ICL-bio 94.5. Llama-3.1-8B: relevant 74.8, ICL-bio 81.0. BBH average GPT-3.5: relevant 63.2, N/A 61.9, random-diff 56.4.
quote: the accuracy of self-generated examples is the key factor
limits: Relevance helped on BBH but not on GSM8K or MATH. Authors' own numbers. 'Relevant' is the Yasunaga-style prompt.
agent_relevance: Check accuracy of a library entry first, relevance second. Test relevance at equal tokens before paying for retrieval.

source: Liu et al. (2025, ICML) What makes in-context learning effective for mathematical reasoning
finding: One demo can lift or hurt. Gain depends on semantic similarity to the test item and on model stability on the demo. A rejection rule that falls back to zero-shot helps.
numbers: One-shot LMS3: Llama2-13B GSM8K 0.414 to 0.447, MATH 0.096 to 0.124. Llama3-8B GSM8K 0.820 to 0.837, MATH 0.324 to 0.353. One-shot failed on 1.83%-34.96% of problems solved zero-shot. GPT-4 MATH zero-shot 0.758 vs LMS3 0.752.
quote: few-shot demonstrations can sometimes bring negative performance
limits: Selection tuned on Llama3-8B; no gain on GPT-4 MATH. Best rejection threshold about the top 10%.
agent_relevance: Examples can break a solved item. Add a rule: if no library entry is close enough, use none (G1, G7).

source: Learning by analogy: computational-graph retrieval for few-shot math prompting (2024)
finding: Retrieving worked examples with similar solution structure beat retrieving by wording and beat random pick, most for small models.
numbers: Exact match averaged over six math sets, k=8: 0.5B random/semantic/graph 18.6/27.6/34.3; 8B/7B 59.7/66.2/68.8; 70B/72B 66.3/72.8/74.4. math_qa: semantic slightly better (27.3 vs 26.6).
limits: Needs a retriever trained on 25% of Math23k. Gap to semantic shrinks with size (+6.7 to +1.6).
agent_relevance: Index the subgoal library by solution structure (the steps), not problem text. Benefit is biggest for weaker solvers.

source: Didolkar et al. (2024) Metacognitive capabilities of LLMs: an exploration in mathematical problem solving
finding: GPT-4 named a skill for each training problem, clustered into 22 (GSM8K) and 117 (MATH) labels, then solved test items using worked examples that carry the named skill. This is a subgoal library in practice.
numbers: MATH: skill-based CoT +11.6% over CoT, +3.5% over complex CoT, +3.5% over topic-based. GSM8K GPT-4-0613: CoT 93.00, CoT+random 92.87, skill-based 94.31, maj@5 95.38. GPT-3.5: retrieval 76.8, skill-based 82.03. Program-aided prompts on MATH subset +7.52% over PAL. 8-shot.
limits: Labels from a strong model; weaker labellers (GPT-3.5, Mixtral) labelled worse. Gain on GSM8K for GPT-4 is only about 1.3 points.
agent_relevance: Closest published match to our subgoal library: label skills, store solved examples under each label, retrieve by label. Random exemplars gave no gain (92.87 vs 93.00), so keep that control.

source: Weitekamp et al. (2025) TutorGym: a testbed for evaluating AI agents as tutors and students
finding: LLM agents given tutor feedback as in-context examples produced error curves similar in shape to human learning curves. Authors think examples teach interface order, not new math.
numbers: 30 tutor domains, 3-10 problems each, human data from 192 learners, five simulated runs per model (Haiku 3.5, GPT-4o). Prompt capped at 50k characters (about 20-30 example states).
quote: primarily provide information on the location and order of answer entry
limits: Similarity is qualitative; no fit statistic in the section read. Authors say in-context learning is arguably not learning.
agent_relevance: Worked examples may fix format and order rather than skill. Test that directly before treating the library as knowledge.

source: Gupta et al. (2025) Beyond final answers: evaluating large language models for math tutoring
finding: LLMs solve college algebra well but tutoring dialogs often contain errors. Good solving does not guarantee correct worked explanations.
numbers: Final-answer accuracy on 110 problems: GPT-3.5 77.3, GPT-4 74.5, GPT-4o 97.3, o1-mini 91.8, o1-preview 85.5. 150 dialogs: 90% high quality but only 56.6% fully correct; GPT-4o about 75%. Cohen kappa 0.85 (quality), 0.82 (correctness). Six dialogs had a right final answer with wrong substeps.
limits: Role-played students, one platform, two reviewers. Not a learning-gain study.
agent_relevance: Do not trust a model-written worked solution because the answer is right. Check each stored step with code before it enters the library.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Decomposing the enigma: subgoal-based demonstration learning for formal theorem proving
finding: Subgoal-structured proofs in the demonstrations raised miniF2F pass rate. A diffusion model reordered the demos.
numbers: miniF2F valid/test: DSP (540B Minerva) 42.6/38.9; this method 48.0/45.5 (valid is cumulative). Ablation test: no subgoal and no diffusion 38.5; no subgoal 40.6; no diffusion 44.3; full 45.5. gpt-3.5-turbo-0301; 20 LLM calls vs 100 for DSP (38.5% at 20 calls).
limits: Abstract figures mix valid and test columns. Formal proving, not word problems. Diffusion trained on evaluated statements.
agent_relevance: Best direct evidence that subgoal structure inside demonstrations helps: about +2 test points from subgoals, about +1.2 from ordering.

source: Notes to Self: can LLMs benefit from experiential abstractions? (2026)
finding: A library of short strategy notes and cautions, built from the model's own solved and failed MATH traces and retrieved at test time, helped one model and hurt another.
numbers: MATH-500 pass@1: Llama-3.2-3B baseline 43.11, inference-time notes 46.42; Qwen-2.5-1.5B 50.23 to 49.14. GRPO with notes in training prompts only: Llama 49.45 (+6.34), Qwen 53.44 (+3.21). Notes at train and test: 47.65 and 52.66. Top-6 notes, dedup at cosine 0.85. Gemma models lost accuracy with notes or blank templates.
limits: Two small models, one RL epoch, no sensitivity analysis. Read via a summary page, so check against the paper before citing.
agent_relevance: Cautions from failures belong in the library too. Test-time injection can hurt solved items, so gate use by a signal (G1).

source: Yang et al. (2024) Buffer of Thoughts: thought-augmented reasoning with LLMs
finding: A meta-buffer of reusable thought templates distilled from solved problems is retrieved and instantiated per task, like a schema library of worked examples.
numbers: GPT-4: Game of 24 standard 3.0, CoT 11.0, ToT 74.0, BoT 82.4; MGSM 84.4 vs 89.2; multi-step arithmetic 84.0 vs 99.8; claimed 12% of the cost of multi-query methods.
limits: Authors' own benchmark choices. Templates are closer to programs than human worked examples.
agent_relevance: Template library plus instantiation already works inside an agent loop. The cost claim bears on G7.

source: Practice less, explain more: LLM-supported self-explanation in calculus (2026)
finding: Students who wrote open-ended self-explanations with LLM feedback did better on explanation quality for transfer problems, but not on the overall post-test.
numbers: N=92, three conditions, 60 minutes. Transfer explanation quality +11.9 points vs control (p=.030); all open-ended explanations +7.3% (p=.057); multiple-choice transfer p=.183. Open-ended group solved fewer practice problems.
limits: Model not named in the text read; group sizes not given; several outcomes with no stated correction.
agent_relevance: Human evidence that LLM-fed self-explanation gives small, narrow gains. Do not promise large effects.

source: ChatGPT-generated help vs human tutor-authored help on mathematics skills (PLOS ONE 2024)
finding: Search summary: only ChatGPT-help beat no help, equal to human-authored help; ChatGPT help failed quality checks on 32% of problems.
numbers: 32% quality failure rate (summary only).
limits: Not opened: 403 on fetch. Do not cite numbers until read.
agent_relevance: Supports a screening step for model-written help.

source: Evaluating LLM-generated worked examples in an introductory programming course (ACE 2024)
finding: Title seen in a search only.
numbers: None read.
limits: Not opened: 403 on fetch.
agent_relevance: Follow up before citing.

source: TeachBench: syllabus-grounded framework for evaluating teaching ability in LLMs (2026)
finding: Search summary: teacher agents shifted from syllabus-grounded instruction to example-driven explanation when example problems were provided.
numbers: None read.
limits: Not opened; summary only.
agent_relevance: Worked examples may pull a model off its plan; keep the plan in code.

source: LLM-drafted explanations of Java worked examples (NSF PAR record)
finding: Search summary: LLM explanations scored high on correctness but lower on completeness, conciseness and specificity.
numbers: Scores not read.
limits: Not opened; summary only.
agent_relevance: Add a completeness check for stored steps.

source: Yasunaga et al. (2024) scale analysis
finding: Self-generated exemplars lose to retrieved labelled exemplars on small models and win on large ones.
numbers: GSM8K across text-curie-001, davinci-001, -002, -003: few-shot CoT with labelled exemplars better at curie-001 and davinci-001; self-generation better at davinci-002 and davinci-003. Self-generation beat 0-shot and 0-shot CoT at every scale.
limits: Old model family. Scores read from scrambled PDF text, so only the ordering is recorded.
agent_relevance: Pick the library source by solver strength: curated entries for weak solvers, self-made for strong ones.

source: Wang et al. (2023) coherence and relevance ablations
finding: Removing relevance of the exemplar to the query cut accuracy to below plain prompting; breaking step order cut it by more than half.
numbers: text-davinci-002 GSM8K: no relevance 11.0 (standard 15.4), no coherence 23.1, no relevance for bridging objects 27.5, no coherence for language templates 25.8, valid CoT 48.5.
limits: Same single model and manually built corruptions. Bamboogle shows smaller drops (23.9 to 39.4).
agent_relevance: A badly matched worked example is worse than none. Gate retrieval on match.

source: Gwak et al. (2026) repeat control
finding: Simply repeating the decoupled example inside the prompt did not recover the integrated gain, so the effect is not just position or salience.
numbers: Repeat prompting on GPT-4o: 52.16% GSM8K and 33.68% MATH, near zero-shot (49.89 and 33.33) and below integrated (54.59 and 37.86).
limits: One model for this control. Preprint.
agent_relevance: Making the model write the analogue is a real step. Keep it as an operator and not as pasted text.

source: Liu et al. (2025) rejection mechanism ablation
finding: With rejection switched off (lambda=100%), LMS3 accuracy sometimes fell below zero-shot. Authors say best lambda is basically within 10%.
numbers: One worked case: best demo ranked in the top 1.19%, above the lambda=1% cut, so LMS3 used zero-shot and kept the correct answer.
limits: Hyperparameter chosen per backbone; Llama3 accuracy fell steadily as lambda grew.
agent_relevance: A similarity floor for using the library is cheap and measurable.

source: Didolkar et al. (2024) cross-model use
finding: Skill labels and exemplars made by GPT-4 were used to prompt Mixtral 8x7B and other maths sets, with reported gains.
numbers: Authors report skill-based exemplars improve Mixtral and transfer to other datasets, and a 4.0% gain over CoT with self-consistency in one setting. Exact Mixtral numbers not recorded here.
limits: Numbers for Mixtral not extracted; only the claim is recorded.
agent_relevance: A library built by a strong model can serve a weaker solver; verify with our own test.

source: Wei et al. (2022) exemplar-sampling check
finding: Results held for three random sets of eight GSM8K training exemplars, so the effect is not tied to one hand-written set.
numbers: PaLM 540B, standard prompting on GSM8K 17.9 vs CoT 56.9; additional gains on MAWPS-style tasks up to 93.3 with CoT.
limits: Variation between annotators and sets still shifted accuracy; small models do not gain.
agent_relevance: Expect variance across example sets; test more than one.
